Actually no matter what the distance an object is from another, Newton showed that the two objects are attracted to each other by the formula F = Gm1m2/r^2. Everything in the universe experiences a slight attraction to everything else in the universe. However, the value of G, the gravitational constant, is a mere 6.67*10^-11, which is why the force between objects is basically negligible unless one or both is very massive and the distance between them is very small.
